title: Season 1, Ep 7: Private model hosting
oneliner: Hosting LLMs on-premises for security and governance must still deliver public-cloud-grade uptime with zero data leakage - and he offers a free reference architecture for it.
says: Transitioning from classic to AI infrastructure architect means knowing how to host an LLM on-premises with uptime comparable to the public cloud. When you host on-premises for security and governance reasons, the architecture must match public-cloud availability and guarantee zero data leakage. He offers the architecture diagram free - comment 'private' to get it.
explained: Private hosting exists because some data simply cannot leave the building - regulated industries, trade secrets, sovereign requirements. The open-weight models from his GPT-OSS reel make it possible; this episode is about making it serious. The bar he sets is the right one: the moment you self-host, you own the reliability the cloud provider used to own - redundancy, failover, capacity - and 'it is down again' kills the program faster than any security audit.

Zero data leakage is the other half of the design: network isolation, no telemetry to external services, access control around the model endpoints. The two requirements pull against each other - availability wants distribution, containment wants walls - and resolving that tension is precisely the architecture work. His diagram giveaway makes this the season's most tangible episode.
takeaway: Self-hosting LLMs = accepting cloud-grade reliability as your own problem, in exchange for total data control. Design for both or expect neither.
